title: Gran Colombia
capsule: Gran Colombia (officially República de Colombia) was the state created by Simón Bolívar and Francisco de Paula Santander following independence from Spain, formally constituted by the Congress of Angostura in 1819 and given a constitution at Cúcuta in 1821. At its greatest extent it incorporated present-day Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, Panama, and parts of northern Peru and northwestern Brazil, representing the largest state in South America at the time. Deep disagreements over centralism versus federalism, regional identities, and the ambitions of Bolívar and José Antonio Páez led to Venezuela's secession in 1829, Ecuador's in 1830, and Bolívar's resignation and death the same year; the rump state officially dissolved at the Convention of 1832, with the successor state retaining the name New Granada.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territory is well documented by treaty and constitutional texts; peripheral jungle and Amazonian frontiers were claimed but not effectively administered, and precise boundary lines were disputed with Peru and Brazil from the outset.
